title: Early-Payment Discount Reinstatement Citing a Prior Courtesy
scenario_text:
You manage accounts receivable at Bramwell Retail. Wholesale customer Hollow Oak Markets short-paid a $210,000 invoice by taking the 2% early-payment discount ($4,200), but their payment arrived 12 days after the discount window closed. They are asking you to honor the discount they already deducted.

Active policy: Cash Application & Discounts Policy CAD-3, effective 2024-06-01. The 2% early-payment discount applies only if the full payment is received within the 10-day discount window. If a customer takes the discount but pays outside the window, the deducted amount is rebilled. Reinstating an improperly taken discount requires a documented Bramwell invoicing or remittance-processing error; customer relationship or retention concerns are explicitly listed as non-qualifying reasons.

The account manager forwards a prior record: on 2024-03-22, AR Manager Owen Frost reinstated a $3,600 discount for Hollow Oak that had been taken 8 days late. The approval memo reads verbatim: "One-time goodwill reinstatement to smooth over a billing-portal complaint. This accommodation is non-binding and non-precedential; it does not entitle Hollow Oak to keep discounts taken outside the window in the future. Logged for audit."

Current facts: AR confirms the invoice was issued correctly and the customer's remittance was received and applied on time internally; there was no Bramwell error. Hollow Oak's stated reason is "we always take the 2%." The account manager argues, "We let it slide last spring, so rebilling now is inconsistent and will annoy them."
question: Should the improperly taken early-payment discount be honored, and on what basis? Give the decision and the controlling reason in one short phrase.
